core_obligations: Flatness of the terms (proof lines 3516-3518): by the cited result on pullbacks of flat modules, each term f^*K^n is a flat O'-module, which gives the second assertion of the statement.

Reduce to a test complex (proof lines 3518-3561): to prove K-flatness one has to show that Tot(f^*K^bullet tensor M^bullet) is acyclic for every acyclic complex M^bullet of O'-modules; choosing a suitable diagram of complexes, the author reduces this to the acyclicity of the complexes obtained by truncating f^*K^bullet, each of which is handled by the auxiliary flatness results of the section.

Finish with the truncation argument (proof lines 3564-3582): assuming K^bullet acyclic as well as K-flat with flat terms, the auxiliary lemma guarantees that the terms of the truncations tau_{<= n}K^bullet are flat, and the induction over n gives that Tot(f^*K^bullet tensor M^bullet) is acyclic, which is the K-flatness of f^*K^bullet.
The counted proof uses an auxiliary commutative diagram of complexes in the Xy-pic format; it is delivered verbatim.
proof_roadmap: Pull back the terms: flatness of K^n gives flatness of f^*K^n.
To get K-flatness, test against an acyclic complex M^bullet of O'-modules.
Reduce the acyclicity of the total tensor product to the truncations of f^*K^bullet, whose terms are flat by the auxiliary result.
Conclude by the induction over the truncations.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that pulling back a K-flat complex with flat terms along a morphism of ringed topoi yields a K-flat complex with flat terms (statement lines 3507-3514). The proof separates the two assertions: flatness of the terms is immediate from the corresponding statement for modules (proof lines 3516-3518), while K-flatness requires testing against arbitrary acyclic complexes and then reducing, through a diagram of complexes set up by the author, to the truncations of f^*K^bullet, whose terms are flat by the auxiliary results of the section, so that an induction over the truncations gives the acyclicity that defines K-flatness (proof lines 3518-3582). The non-formal content is the reduction to the truncations together with the auxiliary flatness of their terms. The claim is H2: a proof with one reduction and one induction, both written out.
